title: Launch and diagnostic: close reading routines
essential_question: How can understanding independent reading, discussion, and evidence help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Activate prior knowledge about close reading routines, surface initial thinking without penalty, and establish the unit question.

Check, revise, or improve work about close reading routines using stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about close reading routines.

The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “close reading routines.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Read or listen closely, annotate or notice craft, discuss evidence, and create a written or spoken response for a real purpose. Keep the explanation centered on close reading routines. Name the success criteria and model how to check work or evidence.
Complete two supported examples or source-based tasks about close reading routines. After each step, ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that move?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of close reading routines and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about close reading routines; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of close reading routines and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about close reading routines; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for close reading routines, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for close reading routines works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of close reading routines, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking close reading routines mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use annotations, discussion notes, reading response, writing sample, revision, and transfer to a new text; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply close reading routines under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Offer an alternate text or private response when content is personally sensitive.
Do not require autobiographical disclosure; fictionalized or analytical alternatives are always acceptable.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting close reading routines.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

essential_question: How can understanding argument, claims, and reasoning help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Activate prior knowledge about claim quality, surface initial thinking without penalty, and establish the unit question.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of claim quality.
Check, revise, or improve work about claim quality using stated success criteria.
success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about claim quality.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Present a brief, accessible prompt connected to “claim quality.” Ask the learner to notice, predict, estimate, recall, or pose a question before instruction.

Read or listen closely, annotate or notice craft, discuss evidence, and create a written or spoken response for a real purpose. Keep the explanation centered on claim quality. Name the success criteria and model how to check work or evidence.
Complete two supported examples or source-based tasks about claim quality. After each step, ask: “What evidence or reasoning supports that move?” Fade prompts on the second example.
Learner completes a new application of claim quality and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about claim quality; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.

student_activity: Learner completes a new application of claim quality and records both the result and the reasoning, evidence, process, or design choice that produced it.
formative_check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about claim quality; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence/reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid approaches when they meet the criteria. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for claim quality, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item.
Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for claim quality works before continuing.
Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of claim quality, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review.
Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking claim quality mastered.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Use annotations, discussion notes, reading response, writing sample, revision, and transfer to a new text; require accurate independent evidence and successful transfer or retrieval on at least two occasions when feasible.
extension: Apply claim quality under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Offer an alternate text or private response when content is personally sensitive.
Do not require autobiographical disclosure; fictionalized or analytical alternatives are always acceptable.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting claim quality.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

extension: Apply reflection and goal setting under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Offer an alternate text or private response when content is personally sensitive.
Do not require autobiographical disclosure; fictionalized or analytical alternatives are always acceptable.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting reflection and goal setting.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

parent_or_guardian_visibility: Share the lesson target, completion state, evidence type, and next instructional step. Do not expose raw private reflections, raw answers, voice recordings, or diagnosis language. For safety-critical tasks, record only the needed guardian confirmation.
home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of reflection and goal setting in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, or private disclosure is required.
